subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which statement about electronegativity across Period 3 (Na to Cl) is correct?
questions.explain: Electronegativity increases across a period because nuclear charge rises while atomic radius falls, so bonding electrons are attracted more strongly.

questions.q: Which statement about the 4s and 3d sub-shells is correct?
options: 4s fills first and 3d empties first on ionisation
4s fills first but 4s empties first on ionisation
questions.explain: 4s fills before 3d during the build-up, yet 4s electrons are removed before 3d electrons when the atom is ionised.

questions.q: What is the empirical formula of a compound containing 40% C, 6.7% H and 53.3% O by mass? (Ar: C=12, H=1, O=16)
questions.explain: Dividing by Ar gives ratios 3.33 : 6.7 : 3.33 = 1 : 2 : 1, so the empirical formula is CH2O.

questions.q: What is the shape of a sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) molecule?
questions.explain: SF6 has 6 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs, giving an octahedral shape with 90° bond angles.

questions.q: 25.0 cm3 of a NaOH solution requires 22.5 cm3 of 0.100 mol/dm3 HCl for neutralisation (1:1). What is the NaOH concentration?
questions.explain: Moles HCl = 0.100 × 22.5/1000 = 0.00225 mol = moles NaOH; concentration = 0.00225/0.0250 = 0.0900 mol/dm3.

questions.q: How many moles of HCl are in 50.0 cm3 of 0.200 mol/dm3 solution?
What is the electron configuration of an Fe2+ ion (Fe is Z = 26)?
questions.explain: When transition metals ionise, the 4s electrons are lost before any 3d electrons, giving Fe2+ as [Ar] 3d6.

questions.q: Which of these molecules is polar overall?
questions.explain: H2O is bent, so its bond dipoles do not cancel, giving a net dipole; the other three are symmetrical and non-polar.

questions.q: Why is the second ionisation energy of any element always greater than its first?
options: The nuclear charge increases after ionisation
The second electron is removed from a positive ion, so it is held more strongly by the same nuclear charge over fewer electrons
The second electron is removed from a larger atom
Shielding increases after the first electron is removed
questions.explain: After the first electron leaves, the remaining electrons are pulled in by an unchanged nuclear charge with reduced repulsion, so more energy is needed.

questions.q: A sample of magnesium gives mass-spectrum peaks at m/z = 24, 25 and 26 with abundances 79.0%, 10.0% and 11.0%. What is the relative atomic mass to 1 d.p.?
During electron impact ionisation in a mass spectrometer, what happens to the sample particles?
options: They are split into protons and neutrons
They are accelerated without any charge change
They gain an electron to form negative ions
A high-energy electron knocks out an electron, forming a 1+ positive ion
questions.explain: A high-energy electron from an electron gun knocks an electron off each particle, typically forming 1+ ions.

questions.q: In the mass spectrum of a molecule, which peak corresponds to the molecular ion?
options: The peak with the highest m/z value (ignoring isotope peaks), equal to the relative molecular mass
The peak at the lowest m/z value
questions.explain: The molecular ion peak is the one at the highest m/z (the M peak), and its value equals the relative molecular mass.

questions.q: The ion CO3^2- has which shape?
questions.explain: The carbonate ion has 3 bonding regions around the central carbon and no lone pairs on it, giving a trigonal planar shape (120°).

questions.q: What is the full electron configuration of a chromium atom (Z = 24) in its ground state?
questions.explain: Chromium adopts 3d5 4s1 because a half-filled d sub-shell with a singly-occupied 4s gives extra stability.

questions.q: Which sub-shell is filled immediately after the 3p sub-shell when building up electron configurations?
questions.explain: 4s is at a lower energy than 3d in the filling sequence, so 4s fills before 3d.

questions.q: How many unpaired electrons are there in a ground-state nitrogen atom (Z = 7)?
questions.explain: Nitrogen is 1s2 2s2 2p3, and the three 2p electrons occupy separate orbitals singly, giving three unpaired electrons.

questions.q: In a time-of-flight mass spectrometer, two ions are accelerated to the same kinetic energy. Which reaches the detector first?
options: The ion with the greater charge always arrives first regardless of mass
The ion with the smaller mass
Both arrive at the same time
The ion with the larger mass
questions.explain: For equal kinetic energy, the lighter ion has a greater velocity and so a shorter time of flight.

questions.q: Which intermolecular force is responsible for the relatively high boiling point of HF compared with HCl?
questions.explain: HF forms hydrogen bonds because hydrogen is bonded to highly electronegative fluorine, raising its boiling point above HCl.

questions.q: Which ion has the electron configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6 3s2 3p6 (i.e. that of argon)?
questions.explain: Ca2+ (Z = 20, losing two electrons) has 18 electrons giving the argon configuration; Na+, Mg2+ and Al3+ all have the neon configuration.

questions.q: What is the bond angle in the molecule XeF4 (square planar)?
questions.explain: XeF4 has 4 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs (octahedral arrangement), giving a square planar shape with 90° F–Xe–F angles.

questions.q: What is the shape of an s orbital?
questions.explain: An s orbital is spherically symmetrical about the nucleus.

questions.q: What is the bond angle between two equatorial bonds in a molecule of PF5?
questions.explain: PF5 is trigonal bipyramidal; the three equatorial bonds lie in a plane at 120° to each other.

questions.q: How many orbitals are present in a p sub-shell, and what shape are they?
questions.explain: A p sub-shell has three dumb-bell-shaped orbitals (px, py, pz) at right angles to each other.

questions.q: What mass of NaOH (Mr = 40) is required to make 2.00 dm3 of 0.25 mol/dm3 solution?
What is the relative charge and relative mass of an electron (to the usual approximation)?
questions.explain: An electron has a relative charge of -1 and a relative mass of about 1/1836 of a proton.

questions.q: What is the predicted bond angle in a molecule of H2O?
questions.explain: Water has 2 bonding pairs and 2 lone pairs; lone-pair repulsion reduces the bond angle to about 104.5°.

questions.q: Which species contains a dative (coordinate) covalent bond?
questions.explain: In NH4+ one N–H bond forms because the lone pair on nitrogen is donated to an H+ ion, making it a dative covalent bond.

questions.q: A 4.0 g sample of magnesium (Ar=24) reacts completely. How many moles of Mg is this?
questions.explain: Moles = mass/Ar = 4.0/24 = 0.167 mol.

questions.q: What volume of 2.0 mol/dm3 stock solution is needed to make 500 cm3 of 0.50 mol/dm3 solution by dilution?
What is the concentration of a solution made by dissolving 0.5 mol of NaCl in water to give 250 cm3 of solution?
questions.explain: Concentration = moles/volume = 0.5 / 0.250 = 2 mol/dm3.
